title: s33 RE-DECONVOLUTION WITH THE EXTREME ROWS: the convex |M| curvature at 1e8G/3e8G/5e8G PULLS THE g-side WINDOW UP - P1 pole best at h0 = 2e10G (max|res| 2.8e5, ~1e-4 relative at the 5e8G row), P3 lognormal best at 1e11G (2.75e5), admissible h0 compressed from the s29 window [2e8G, 1e11G] to ~[1e10G, 1e12G] with best fits at the upper edge; the position-amplitude degeneracy survives but narrows to ~2 decades, and the row needed to break it moves to t ~ 3e20..3e21 - breaking it is now definitively an engine task (C zeta channel or more RAM), not a data task on this machine
body: DATA MILESTONE (no RH claim): the s29 pin family re-ran (s33_redec_extreme.py, same machinery, same grid L2000/1/n160, same part structure) with the s30 far-extreme census rows added to the far set (36 rows total: 16 near <2.2G, 15 far >=2e3G incl. the staggered 5e8G row, max t/G = 5e8).  Part A (min-norm e, joint (A,B,e) solve): unchanged verdict from s27/s29 - the min-norm drift is NOT localized at this grid (delta-e support: none above 3e-3); E_above(e) ~ -3.2e22 is dominated by the extreme-row direction (a degenerate near-null direction of the kernel at these heights, not a pinned structure).  Part B (parametric forward fits, FAR rows only, A/B anchored to the near face: A = -2.527100e7, B = +5.238779e8, max near res 1123.82): the measured drift D(t) = M - (A ln t + B) runs from +2.17e5 at 1e6G down to -2.44e9 at 5e8G (the monotone negative far drift, now with three extreme points on it).  P1 pole (1-cell delta): the best max|res| MOVES UP THE g-axis with the new curvature - s29's best was ~1e9G, s33's best is h0 = 2e10G (max|res| = 282516.5, ~1.2e-4 relative at the 5e8G row), and the res is FLAT ~2.9e5 over h0 in [1e10G, 5e11G] before deteriorating (2.3e6 at 5e13G).  P3 lognormal bump: sig=0.50 best 288588 at 1e11G, sig=1.00 best 275145 at 1e11G (s29's best was ~1e9G with sigma ~1).  P2 power tail: q=0 (constant density bump) best 2.3e7 at 1e9G, q=1 (density-fraction shape) flat ~1.94e9 across the window (dominated by the 5e8G row).  READ: the convex curvature of |M| at the extreme rows (the t^2 coefficient +9.59e7 per 1e8G^2, discovery 0096) is the (t/g0)^2 kernel tail of the far-side window, and it PREFERS the upper edge of the s29 window - the g-side window of record UPDATED from [2e8G, 1e11G] (best ~1e9G, amplitude O(1e8..1e11)) to admissible h0 ~ [1e10G, 1e12G] with best fits at h0 ~ 1e10G..1e11G and best-config amplitude O(1e9..1e12).  The position-amplitude degeneracy SURVIVES (the flat res over [1e10G, 5e11G] is the degeneracy re-appearing at the upper edge) but is now ~2 decades instead of ~3-4.  The row that breaks it is a t ~ g0 row at t ~ 3e20..3e21 - ~20x..200x past the verified 1.5e19 boundary, i.e. an ENGINE task (a C Riemann-Siegel channel without the mpf term arrays, or more RAM), not a data task on this 124 GB machine.  Part-A degeneracy + Part-B flat-res are the same phenomenon read two ways: the far rows are a leverage probe, and the extreme curvature pins the LEAD COEFFICIENT of the window (the (t/g0)^2 term) while leaving its CENTER free over ~2 decades.  Outputs: scripts/rh/s33_redec_extreme.py, tmp/s33_run.log (full stdout), tmp/s33_redec_extreme.md (pointer).  Feeds B7 (g-side window of record) and B5 (law territory).  No RH claim.  (Also this stretch: discovery 0096 locked the 5e8G row and moved the boundary to 1.5e19.)
